title: Permissions & Approval Gates
objective: After this lesson you will be able to scope tool permissions per consumer, gate destructive operations with approval flows (including elicitation), and audit permission grants like access-control rules.
why: Exposed tools are powers: lookup leaks data, refunds move money, deletes destroy. Ungated destructive tools turn confused agents into incidents — the support-drafter-with-refunds nightmare from CrewAI Ch.7, now at protocol scale across every host. Permissions (who may call what), gates (approvals before effects), and audit (who did what) are the access-control triple of MCP deployments.

blocks.text: Scopes per consumer, not per server

Permissions attach to **(consumer, tool)** pairs, not servers globally: the support assistant reads orders and drafts; the finance consumer issues gated refunds; the analytics job reads aggregates only. Same server, three scopes. Scope manifests (role → tools, from CrewAI Ch.7) port directly — MCP servers enforce what manifests declare, per connected client identity.

blocks.caption: Default-deny matrices: unlisted pairs refuse loudly

blocks.text: Gated tools pause for human approval via **elicitation** (`elicitation/create`): server requests confirmation/details through the client, user approves/edits/declines, execution proceeds or aborts. Refunds over thresholds, deletions, external sends — anything irreversible or monetary. Elicitation is MCP's native HITL (LangGraph interrupts, CrewAI gates — same pattern, protocol-native). Unknown verdicts fail closed to logged skips.

blocks.caption: Deny/gate/allow with audit on every branch — access control as code

blocks.text: Every tool call appends **consumer, tool, args, verdict, outcome, timestamp** to an append-only log — allowed and denied alike (denied attempts are threat signal). Audit reviews ask: ungated destructives? scope creep per consumer? denied-attempt spikes (attack campaigns)? The log answers all three; missing logs answer nothing. stdout stays protocol-clean; audit flows to stderr/files/sinks.

blocks.title: Enforce the matrix
blocks.note: Run it: expect 5/5 — including unknown consumer (deny), unknown tool (deny), and the finance gate. Default-deny closes both novelty holes by construction.

items: Scopes per (consumer, tool): allow/gate/deny with default-deny closing novelty holes
Gates via elicitation for irreversible/monetary tools; edits re-validated; unknowns fail closed
Append-only audit per call (allowed + denied); denied spikes signal campaigns

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice matrix and confirm 5/5 with both novelty denials. (b) Add an analytics-job scope (order-stats allow, everything else deny) plus a test proving lookup-order denies. (c) Write the elicitation payload for a $500 refund (action, args, context shown to approver) and state the three verdict paths.
hints: Baseline 5/5: allows, deny, gate, unknown-consumer deny, unknown-tool deny — novelty covered both directions.
Analytics scope: {order-stats: allow} only; test asserts lookup-order → deny (default-deny proves itself on additions).
Payload: action issue-refund + args + ticket/policy summary for the approver; verdicts approve (execute) / edit (re-validate then execute) / skip-or-unknown (logged skip).
exercise.why: Novelty-proofing (unknowns deny), scope addition discipline (prove denials on every add), and elicitation design (verdicts with routings) are the three permission judgments — each verified, none assumed.
exercise.code: // Scope-addition protocol: manifest edit → novelty tests → green required.

quiz.q: Support assistant holds ungated issue-refund. Fix?
options: Rescope: deny for support, gate for finance (elicitation over thresholds), audit all paths — least privilege per consumer
quiz.explain: Drafting ≠ executing. Money tools live gated under finance scope; support drafts and recommends. Scopes per pair, default-deny.

quiz.q: Unknown consumer connects requesting delete-user. Behavior?
options: Deny loudly + audit: default-deny closes novelty holes in both directions (unknown who, unknown what)
quiz.explain: Novelty denies by construction: unlisted consumers and unlisted tools both refuse with audit trails. Open-by-default is the breach.

quiz.q: Approval edits the refund amount. Handling?
options: Re-validate edited args against the schema, then execute — edits are fresh untrusted input
quiz.explain: Human edits bypass the original validation context: re-validate like new args. Edits are inputs, not blessings.

summary: Per-pair scopes with default-deny, elicitation gates for destructive power, append-only audit with denied-attempt intelligence. Permissions maintained per change, never assumed.
next: Locked down — now run safely: timeouts, idempotency, isError discipline, and stdout hygiene. Next: execution that survives production.
